gapTheirs: The caret is the only saturated pixel on an otherwise perfectly neutral page: #00B5FF, 6px x 72px (3 x 36 CSS px @2x), which is the full line box — it overhangs cap-top by 18px and the baseline by 23px. B's caret is 4px x 54px (2 x 27 CSS px) in the text's own ink, sitting 12px above cap and 11px below baseline, i.e. fitted to the glyph. A's is 50% fatter, 33% taller, and chromatic; it flags itself instead of marking a position.
verdict: Same typeface, same 36px line, same ink, same margin — so this comes down to whether the type knows what the words are, and B's doesn't. B renders '#', '##', '**' and '-' at full-strength #1C1C1C, so the syntax has more visual weight than the prose it's marking, and a two-heading document reads as one undifferentiated block; you lose your place scrolling because nothing steps. A dims the same markers to #9E9E9E, bolds the heading, and sets a true cursive italic that still holds the monospace advance — the column grid matched B's to the pixel across sixty columns, so nothing jitters as you type. A's cyan full-height caret is a loud, slightly juvenile choice against that restraint, but a caret you dislike costs you a second; a page with no hierarchy costs you every re-read.

states.name: quattro
states.gap: Zero semantic ink. Headings render at exactly body weight and body size — 2357 dark pixels in the same 900×50 band where A's bold H1 has 3377, a ~43% weight deficit — and every marker (#, ##, *, **) is #1C1C1C, the identical hex as the prose, versus A's #9E9E9E. Italic and bold literally never appear: 'Nothing out there is ever in a hurry' is roman, 'bottle' is roman, so a page of B is one undifferentiated grey slab with asterisks shouting at full volume alongside the words.
states.gapTheirs: The caret is the only chromatic ink on the page: #00B5FF, 6 device px wide (3 CSS px) and 72 px tall (36 CSS px — a full line-height on ~17.8px type, overshooting both cap-height and descender), a saturated code-editor accent dropped mid-sentence into an otherwise strictly neutral #1C1C1C-on-#F9F9F9 page. B's caret is #1C1C1C, 4×54 device px (2×27 CSS) — hairline, ink-coloured, and it never pulls the eye off the sentence. Second offence: A's H1 and H2 are pixel-identical in size and weight (same ~29-30px ink band, same bold), so 'The Lighthouse' and 'What the sea keeps' rank the same — you tell them apart by counting hashes.
states.verdict: The metrics are the same file: identical ~17.8px mono, 36px line-height (~2.0), ~71-character measure, full-blank-line paragraph gaps, same #1C1C1C on #F9F9F9 — so this is decided entirely on how the ink is graded, and B doesn't grade it at all. In B, `**bottle**` reads as four asterisks and a word at exactly the same weight and colour as the sentence around it; when you scroll back over a morning's work there is no visual difference between a chapter heading and a line of dialogue, which is exactly the moment a writer loses the shape of the draft. A dims the markers to #9E9E9E, sets a real drawn italic and a real bold, and bolds the headings — the syntax recedes and the prose comes forward, which is the whole point. A's punishment: it undoes that restraint with a fat cyan caret three pixels wide and a full line tall, and it gives H1 and H2 identical treatment, so its hierarchy stops after one step.
secondary: Both pages ink #1C1C1C on #F9F9F9 (~15:1) — harder than a long session wants; ~#2E2E2E would sit easier without going grey

states.name: mono
states.gap: Zero typographic hierarchy: '# The Lighthouse' renders at the same size AND the same 400 weight as body text (2169 dark px vs A's 3493 over the same 340x50 box — 1.6x less ink, 5px stems vs 13px), every marker — #, ##, **, *, - — sits at full #1C1C1C identical to the prose, and neither '*Nothing out there is ever in a hurry,*' nor '**bottle**' picks up italic or bold. The page has one weight, one colour, one size, top to bottom.
states.gapTheirs: The caret is a 6px-wide (3 CSS px) full-line-box bar, 72px tall against a text band that is only 37px from ascender to descender — nearly 2x the type's own height — and it is #00B5FF, the single saturated colour on a page otherwise built from #1C1C1C on #F9F9F9; B's caret is 4px/54px in #1C1C1C, matched to the ink. A's headings also carry no size ladder: H1 and H2 are both the body's 23.8px advance and 37-38px cap band, separated from prose only by weight.
states.verdict: B is a text file in a window: the same 20px regular mono at #1C1C1C for the heading, the prose, the emphasis and the asterisks around it, so the eye has nothing to land on and a section break is announced only by two literal hash characters. A does the one thing that matters here — headings go bold, markers drop to ~#9E9E9E while keeping their monospace advance so the grid never breaks, and the italic is a real cursive italic at full ink rather than a slant, so 'Nothing out there is ever in a hurry' reads as speech instead of as more prose. A's cyan caret is the wrong note — 3 CSS px of #00B5FF spanning the full 36px line box on a page with no other colour, an IDE cursor dropped into a manuscript — and its H1 and H2 are the same size, so the document has weight but no depth. Still not close: B's total flatness costs a writer more on every scroll than A's loud caret costs on one line.
